content.comment_body: I want to measure voltage between 0-2VDC, show it on an operator display with two decimal places (for example, 1.43V), and simultaneously use this measured value to switch an output. Is it possible to use [product_name] for this operation? Having two decimal places displayed is essential.

Displaying values with two decimal places is possible, but only for the visual display, as [product_name] operates with fixed-point numbers. I'll provide an example soon. Keep in mind, though, that [product_name]'s analog input range is 0-10V, so you're measuring in the lower segment of the scale. This means there may be a greater error when reading such low voltages.

analysis.insight_summary: Users aim to measure a 0-2VDC voltage, display it on an operator panel with two decimal places, and use the same value to control outputs. The hardware and software allow two decimal points for display, but computations are limited to fixed-point numbers, which reduces measurement accuracy at lower voltages due to the 0-10V input range. Precise readings can be challenging in the lower part of the range.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the system to display low-voltage analog values with two decimal places and utilize those values for output control, prioritizing accuracy and precision in measurement.
